extracted.intended_audience: scientists, naturalists, physiologists, anthropologists and educated readers of Popular Science Monthly
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and methodological criteria for (a) solving the scientific problems of voluntary motion and the will, and (b) investigating the origin of life (Monera) — plus practical methods for producing composite portraits by optical/photographic superimposition. Targeted at researchers and practitioners devising experiments and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genesis of the power of voluntary motion
rubrics_metrics.description: The genesis of the power of voluntary motion, or its differentiation from some mental power which preceded it; and how it was differentiated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as the first distinct branch that requires full and separate consideration when seeking a scientific solution of the problem of voluntary motion and the will.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evolution of voluntary motion across animal kingdom
rubrics_metrics.description: The evolution of the power of voluntary motion considered as an organic procedure in the entire animal kingdom, by which it was developed from its earliest genesis up to its highest capabilities in man, as the result of such changes in the faculty, from any cause whatever, as were transmissible and transmitted by inheritance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identified as the second distinct branch requiring separate treatment — i.e., comparative/evolutionary study of the faculty across taxa and through inheritance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maturation of voluntary motion in the individual
rubrics_metrics.description: The maturation of the power of voluntary motion considered as an organic procedure in the individual (man, for instance), by which it develops or ripens through the gradations of evolution independently of the operation of any external cause, such as education and experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third branch: study of ontogenetic maturation (internal organic development) distinct from acquisition by practice or education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquisitions added to matured faculty (practice/education)
rubrics_metrics.description: The acquisitions of the power of voluntary motion, or whatever is added to the maturing or matured faculty, by which it is enabled to do with greater ease, freedom, force, or dexterity, what, without evolution and maturation, it could not do at all, and could never be educated to do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fourth branch: treat separately those improvements due to training/experience (acquisitions) rather than inheritance/maturation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physiological equivalence criterion for voluntary vs reflex movement
rubrics_metrics.description: If the final conclusion is true there should be no difference, physiologically, between a voluntary and a reflex movement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument: the essential physiological phenomena (peripheral impression → nerve conduction → nervous centre molecular action → nervous force → muscle contraction) are the same in both voluntary and reflex movements; volition is the molecular action reflected in consciousness and thus cannot determine that molecular action. Use this equivalence as a test for theories of volition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical phase requirement for origin-of-life theories
rubrics_metrics.description: We have to show how life originates and how organization takes its rise (the physical phase of the problem of life).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author calls this the 'physical phase' — demonstrating origin of vitality and the rise of organization is a necessary condition for establishing evolutionary continuity from inorganic to organic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Psychical phase requirement: motion ↔ sensation identity
rubrics_metrics.description: We must demonstrate how the state called feeling is related to motion, i.e., establish either the essential identity of motion and sensation or the gradual transformation of one into the other (the psychical phase).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To vindicate evolution as a monistic system, show how inner sensation can arise from outer motion or how the two are continuously related; this constitutes the psychical phase to be addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physico-psychical phase requirement: origin of feeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstration of the specific conditions of organization which constitute the starting-point of feeling or subjective experience (the physico-psychical phase of the problem of life).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intermediate task: identify organizational conditions at which subjective feeling first appears during evolution — necessary to bridge physical organization and psychical experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological criterion: study the least complicated forms of life (Monera)
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct attention to the study of vitality in its least complicated forms, which manifest the properties of life and at the same time do not confuse us with structural entanglements; e.g., Monera — homogeneous flakes or globules of viscid material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasoning: simplest living forms show fundamental properties (movement, nourishment, reaction, reproduction) without morphological complications; thus they are the most promising starting point for investigating origin of life and the conditions for feeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid organisms with fixed differentiated parts for origin-of-life work
rubrics_metrics.description: Wherever we find fixity of differentiated parts already established, there the difficulty begins — the organism gains the appearance of a mechanical contrivance and confuses origin investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides subject selection: prefer organisms lacking stable differentiated morphology to avoid misleading mechanical complexity when searching for life's origin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extract typical characteristics by optical superimposition (composite portraits principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Having obtained drawings or photographs of several persons alike in most respects, but differing in minor details, extract the typical characteristics by superimposing optically the various drawings and accepting the aggregate result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principle proposed by Galton and Spencer: superimposition yields an 'average' or typical visage; intended as a method to extract typical features from multiple similar portraits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent-paper tracing and transmitted-light superposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings reduced to the same scale might be traced on separate pieces of transparent paper and secured one upon another, then held between the eye and the light to obtain the aggregate result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical technique (Spencer suggestion) for achieving optical superposition without photographic apparatus — useful for manual composite construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographic multiple exposure to form composite portraits
rubrics_metrics.description: Throw faint images of the several portraits, in succession, upon the same sensitized photographic plate to produce a composite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Galton's photographic implementation: successive faint exposures on the same plate produce an averaged composite image; recommended for those with access to photography.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use stereoscopic optics to superimpose portraits
rubrics_metrics.description: It is perfectly easy to superimpose optically two portraits by means of a stereoscope, and a person used to handle instruments will find a common double eye-glass fitted with stereoscopic lenses almost as effectual and handier than shop stereoscope boxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative optical implementation: stereoscope or modified spectacles can be used to superimpose images for rapid visual averaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanical tracing of sectional outlines for superposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Mr. Spencer devised an instrument for tracing mechanically longitudinal, transverse, and horizontal sections of heads on transparent paper, intending to superimpose them and to obtain an average result by transmitted light.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation to use mechanical tracing of standardized sectional outlines to align and superimpose head profiles accurately for composite portrait construction.
